interface.title: Thresholdmann
interface.stage_of_work: Preprocessing: brain extraction / tissue masking of a 3D MRI volume before downstream analysis
interface.what_it_is_for: Interactively building a space-varying intensity threshold from control points placed on a 3D MRI volume to segment the brain, then exporting the mask and the control points for scripted reuse.

data.note: First loaded bear_uchar.nii.gz (225x328x210 voxels, 0.33 mm) through the Choose file picker. Later reloaded the same volume with the built-in 'MRI from a Sloth bear' demo button (file shown as img/bear_uchar.nii.gz). The viewer always starts with one control point at the volume centre (112,164,105), value 127.

tree.general: Separate the object of interest from its background in a 3D image volume using a threshold that changes across space, and export the result
tree.specific: Segment the brain in an MRI NIfTI volume with an adaptive threshold surface built from control points, then save mask.nii.gz and control-points.json

features.name: Volume loader with bundled example and file information panel
features.general: Bring a 3D image volume into the tool from a local file or a bundled example dataset, and show its basic header facts (file name, dimensions, voxel size) so the user can confirm the right data loaded.
features.specific: A Choose file picker (and a drop zone, not tried) accepts .nii/.nii.gz. The 'MRI from a Sloth bear' button loads img/bear_uchar.nii.gz. The Information box shows file, dim (225 x 328 x 210) and pixdim (0.33). Every load starts with one control point at the volume centre, value 127.
steps: Press Choose and pick a .nii.gz file, or press the bundled example button
Wait for the sagittal view to appear
Read file, dim and pixdim in the Information box to confirm the volume
(Unverified) drag a NIfTI file onto the drop zone instead

features.name: Control-point editor on a slice viewer, with a linked point table
features.general: Place, move, delete and select landmark points on a 2D slice of a 3D volume. A synced table lists each point's coordinates, and clicking a row jumps the viewer to that point's slice.
features.specific: Choose the Select/Move/Add/Remove tool (or press s/m/a/r), then click or drag on the stereotaxic slice. The right-hand table shows I/J/K for each point. Clicking a row highlights the point and moves the viewer to its slice.
steps: Choose the Add tool (button or the 'a' key) and click the slice to place a point
Choose Move (button or the 'm' key) and drag a point; its I/J/K in the table updates
Choose Select and click a table row to jump to that point's slice
Choose Remove (button or the 'r' key) and click a point to delete it and its row
serves_tasks: Add a local reference point where the image is darker or brighter, and give it its own threshold
Go to a chosen reference point

features.name: Space-varying threshold from per-point values, with live mask preview
features.general: Give each landmark its own cutoff value. The values are blended smoothly across space into a threshold field, and the binary mask on the image updates live.
features.specific: Each control point row has a Value slider and a number box (0–255). Changing it recomputes the threshold surface, and the red Threshold Mask overlay updates at once. A new point takes the value of the last-edited point. The number box is too narrow for 3-digit values (173 shows as '17'); read the slider or the saved JSON.
steps: Add a point in a region that is too dark or too bright
Drag its row slider or type a value into its number box
Watch the mask grow or shrink around that point only
Repeat for other regions until the boundary is right everywhere
serves_tasks: Add a local reference point where the image is darker or brighter, and give it its own threshold

features.name: Overlay view toggle: binary mask vs. threshold field
features.general: Switch the display between the binary segmentation result and the underlying spatial threshold field, to see where each landmark pulls the cutoff up or down.
features.specific: Threshold Mask shows the red overlay on the MRI; Threshold Value shows the interpolated threshold surface as greyscale (darker near low-value points).
steps: Press Threshold Value to see the threshold field
Check where each control point raises or lowers the field
Press Threshold Mask to return to the red overlay
serves_tasks: View the threshold field itself instead of the mask

features.name: Selection polarity switch: keep above or below the threshold
features.general: Choose which side of the threshold counts as the object, so the same tool works for images where the object is brighter or darker than its surroundings.
features.specific: Select Up keeps voxels brighter than the threshold (T1-like); Select Down keeps darker ones (T2-like). The mask overlay, Render 3D and Save Mask all follow this setting.
steps: Press Select Down to keep voxels below the threshold
Check the inverted mask on the slice
Press Select Up to keep voxels above the threshold again
serves_tasks: Choose whether to keep the voxels above or below the threshold

features.name: Three-plane slice viewer with display controls
features.general: Browse a 3D volume one slice at a time in three orthogonal planes. Adjust the overlay opacity and the image contrast and brightness to judge a segmentation boundary.
features.specific: Sagittal/Axial/Coronal buttons and a slice slider (the slice index is shown as I:/J:/K:). Three left-panel sliders set mask opacity, contrast and brightness.
steps: Choose a plane (Sagittal, Axial, Coronal)
Drag the slice slider to a slice
Raise mask opacity to see the selected region
Adjust contrast and brightness to see faint tissue boundaries
serves_tasks: Browse the volume slice by slice in different planes
Adjust the overlay and the image display so the boundary is easy to judge

features.name: Whole-volume apply with progress, then 3D surface preview
features.general: Apply the current settings to every slice with a progress readout. Show the result as a 3D surface in a separate window.
features.specific: Render 3D runs the threshold over all slices ('Thresholding n out of 225' → 'Done') and opens render3D/index.html with a normal-shaded mesh of the mask.
steps: Press Render 3D
Watch the per-slice progress until it says Done
Switch to the new tab to inspect the brain surface
serves_tasks: Look at the segmented object as a 3D surface
features.note: Screens 021 (progress readout) and 023 (rendered mesh) from the first run show this working; 'not_confirmed' reflects the replay browser's screenshots timing out after 'Computing mesh from segmentation', not a failure. Rotating/zooming the mesh was never captured.

features.name: Export the mask volume and the parameters that made it
features.general: Download the full binary result in the field's standard volume format. Separately, download a small parameter file (point coordinates and values) so the result can be rebuilt or applied in scripts.
features.specific: Save Mask asks for a filename, thresholds all slices and downloads mask.nii.gz (it follows the Select Up/Down setting). Save Control Points downloads control-points.json as {points:[[i,j,k]...], values:[...]}. Load Control Points opens a file picker to read such a file back (unverified: no JSON was ever loaded).
steps: Press Save Control Points and accept the filename prompt
Press Save Mask and wait for the per-slice progress
Accept the 'Save mask as...' prompt to download mask.nii.gz
(Unverified) press Load Control Points to restore the points
serves_tasks: Save the reference points and their values

The state after loading saved control points: the only uploadable test file was the NIfTI, so the Load Control Points picker could not be given a JSON

Loading control points back in: the file picker opened, but there is no JSON test file to give it (downloaded files can't be uploaded)
Drag-and-drop of the NIfTI onto the upload box: the file picker was used instead
Checking what mask.nii.gz contains: it is binary, so only its size (475,129 bytes) could be read
The external links (GitHub, issue tracker, JOSS paper) are outside the allowed host and were not opened
